Deleatidium mayflies are highly intolerant to pHs less than 4, and that their survival in AMD is primarily driven by pH.
Deleatidium mayflies sourced from naturally acidic streams were more tolerant to low pH (3-4) and AMD than mayflies sourced from circumneutral streams.
Deleatidium mayflies sourced from naturally acidic streams are better able to withstand the toxicity of AMD compared to mayflies from circumneutral streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMD toxicity to mayflies was pH-dependent and that the chemistry of natal streams influences the sensitivity of the mayfly Deleatidium to AMD.
the pH of AMD was the most important factor in toxicity to mayflies, but the presence of heavy metals and precipitates at low pH could also have contributed to mortality.
the chemistry of natal streams influences the sensitivity of benthic macroinvertebrates to acid mine drainage, and this should be considered in mine remediation.

the water quality of a natal stream strongly determines the sensitivity of mayfly to acidification.
the chemistry of AMD-impacted streams should be considered in the context of the natural water quality of the receiving stream.
